idiom_name: View pipeline (xs.view.map.filter) forced by .to, or Iterator for single-pass
implementation_notes: Scala's collections library distinguishes strict from non-strict transformers: a view constructs only a proxy for the result collection and its elements get constructed only as they are demanded, so xs.view.map(...).filter(...) performs no intermediate allocation and .to(Seq)/.toList is the explicit force back to a strict collection. Iterator is the single-pass alternative when consumption-once semantics are wanted, and LazyList (formerly Stream) trades memory for memoized repeated access. The views chapter is explicit that views belong in purely functional code: side-effecting transformations under a view have deferred, re-evaluated effects.
code_sketch:
val total = people.view
  .filter(_.age > 18)
  .map(_.score)
  .take(100)
  .sum                       // forces the view once; no intermediate collections
pitfalls: Views are not memoized: every traversal re-runs the whole chain (and any side effect in it), so a view reused twice computes twice.
Views are not thread-safe and not lazy in the memoizing sense; LazyList and Iterator have different reuse semantics - choose deliberately.
A view escaping into a public API leaves callers a proxy whose evaluation happens during their traversal; force with .to at the boundary.
